course_description:
This course critically examines the history of educational research and the ethical considerations necessary to balance the rights and responsibilities of researchers, participants and the community. It considers the epistemological assumptions of widely used research designs and the relationship between research questions and the choice of particular designs. The course explores indepth systematic practices and strategies that can improve the quality of research. The genres within which research is written and the communication of research to a variety of audiences are considered. Students will build their skills and knowledge in the conduct of educational research throughout the course. This course may not be offered in person if the enrolment is less than 10 students.

This is a core course of the Master of Educational Studies program. As indicated by the title, the course is about research methods in education. Methods are tools and strategies that are utilized for collecting information and producing evidence that can serve as a basis for education policy and practice. But the course is not just about the nuts and bolts of research; it is about doing education research in a socially responsive, critically conscious and ethically responsible way. The course takes an innovative approach and emphasizes all key aspects of conducting research including its thinking, reading, doing and writing. It is targeted at three groups of prospective students in the field of education: those who are planning to undertake higher research degrees in the near or distant future; those who are currently teaching or will be teaching in the future and need to develop an understanding of research including a critical consumption of research output which can help in theirﾠpractice; and those who have an inherent interest in research and knowledge construction for its own sake, particularly in the field of education.

The course is divided into threeﾠmodules, with attention to 'writing research' as a fourth area of attention. Theﾠmodules about Designing and Conducting Qualitative and Quantitative researchﾠfocus on methods, strategies and techniques of qualitative and quantitative methods and data. The Ethical Conduct of Research moduleﾠdeals with the emergence and regulation of ethics and doing educational research as an ethical practice.ﾠThe Writing Research materialﾠhas a focus on major research genres, with reference to the quality and strategy of writing and how writing is related to research impact.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand issues around the ethical conduct of research and apply this understanding to educational research;
Demonstrate understanding of the use of qualitative research in education and of the rationale, processes and strategies of collecting and analysing qualitative data;
Critically evaluate the rationale, strategies and techniques of quantitative research design and data analysis
Analyse and compare key writing research genres and discuss their roles in research dissemination and impact
Construct a research proposal that demonstrates and applies your knowledge and understanding of designing a research project in education

assessment_details.title: Assignment 1: Literature Review
assessment_details.task_description: The aim of this assessment task is to help you identify a research topic that you are interested in and for which you would like to develop a detailed research proposal for the final assessment task in this course. You will need to review relevant research studies on your selected topic to provide an adequate justification for the research. This is not an annotated bibliography; your aim should be to critically review the studies, synthesize the findings and draw on these findings to make a case for the proposed topic. This literature review can be used to help inform Assignment 2. Performing this first assessment task successfully will require you to: Specify clearly the research problem/topic/issue that you are proposing to investigate; Review and synthesize relevant, timely and substantive studies; and Identity a ‘gap’ - an under-researched area - in the literature to provide justification for the research. The review should focus on relevant and up-to-date research on the topic. Although a fixed format for the assessment task is not prescribed, it is expected that there will be: * an introduction about the nature of the topic; * a body where the studies will be reviewed and; * a conclusion where justification for the 'gap' in the topic will be provided. assessment_details.title: Assignment 2: Writing a research proposal
assessment_details.task_description: Write a research proposal on a topic of your interest. The research proposal should demonstrate your ability to develop a clear overview of a project, focused on your particular topic. This proposal must reflect an understanding of the nature of 'good' research. In other words, you will be applying what you have learned during the course. The focus of the research proposal is on your ability to APPLY your understanding of particular approaches (qualitative, quantitative, mixed methods) to a specific education topic. Most people will develop their proposal based on the original topic in their first assignment (literature review), but this is not compulsory. The format of the research proposal should be similar to the framework provided and discussed during class. Your submission can include references from the required and recommended readings, but you must include sources/readings beyond the course materials, focused on the specific research methods you have chosen. assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Having completed your research proposal, the last assessment task will provide you with the opportunity to engage with a more experienced researcher in a dialogue with them to show your understanding of the key outcomes of the course as these relate to research proposal development processes. You will be asked a series of questions about your research proposal. You will not know the exact questions, but you should come prepared to explain why you have chosen the topic for your research proposal and the approach you have taken to your research proposal. You can anticipate being asked questions about the overall research design for your research proposal as well as other aspects of the proposal such as methods, ethical issues etc. – as reflected in the learning outcomes of the course. You may have a copy of your research proposal with you during the conversation. Please note: This task is not designed to ‘trick’ you but is instead an opportunity to engage with a more experienced researcher to help further develop your understanding of the research process. The best engagements will be ‘conversations’ where you take the initiative to explain some of the nuances of your work in response to their questions. Each 'in conversation' dialogue will be a 5 - 10 minute interactive online oral demonstration, where targeted questions will be asked throughout by the marker, focused upon explaining the key ideas and justifying choices within your research proposal. The time allocated for each slot is 20 minutes. These live oral dialogues/demonstrations will be video recorded to ensure there is an accurate record of your discussion/performance. Recordings will be retained for 12 months on a secure UQ system in accordance with UQ assessment policy. For internal students, the oral will be held in person with your marker. For external students, this will be an online oral, and you will require a working webcam, headphones, and microphone, and you will be required to reveal the room during the oral. There will be an opportunity to check your equipment in the weeks immediately prior to the oral assignment. This assessment task is to be completed live via the Echo 360 Go-React Platform. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools during the interview will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Introduction and course overview This week's class introduces the course, including an overview of the key topics to be covered each week. For further details, refer to the supporting materials (modules) relating to each week as the course progresses. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Qualitative & Quantitative Research:Context This week, we focus upon the importance of context for informing any kind of research. Learning outcomes: L02, L05

Qualitative Research: Policy Qualitative research exists in a range of formats and is influenced by the broader policy conditions in which research is undertaken. Policy is also an important focus of many kinds of research. Learning outcomes: L02, L05

Methods of Qualitative Research This week, we delve into the range of methods which can be employed as part of qualitative research approaches. This includes more traditional as well as more recent approaches. We will also focus attention upon the nature of literature reviews - the primary focus of your first assignment. Learning outcomes: L02, L05

Qualitative data analysis There are a range of ways in which qualitative data can be analysed. This week, we will consider some of the most common ways such analysis can be undertaken and key factors to keep in mind when analysing such data. Learning outcomes: L02, L05

Conducting Literature Reviews As your first assignment focuses on developing a literature review, we will focus more substantively on the nature of literature reviews this week (although we will be referring to the importance and character of literature reviews throughout the first half of the course, not just this week, and Week 4). We will also begin to consider the nature of quantitative research. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Finalising Literature Review This week's class is a 'drop-in' session (both in-person and online) if people have any last-minute questions they would like to ask before their literature review is due later this week. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Quantitative Research Processes There are many different kinds of quantitative research. This week, we will focus on some of the more common approaches. This week will also involve an interactive Excel data analysis exercise to assist you to better understand the potential of quantitative research approaches. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Mixed Methods A considerable amount of research draws upon both qualitative and quantitative approaches. This week, we will focus on the advantages of working across both quantitative methods and methodologies as part of 'mixed methods' research. Learning outcomes: L03, L05
Break Week This week is the University 'break week'. There will be no classes taught in any of your courses this week.

Ethical Principles and Approaches The class for this week will introduce you to the range of ethics-related principles and broad ethical issues you need to be aware of as you consider how to develop a research plan/proposal, and conduct research. Learning outcomes: L01, L05

Practising Ethics in Educational Research This week builds upon the previous week, with its focus on 'ethical principles', emphasising 'ethics in action'. This week's class will also include attention to, and valuing of, Indigenous-inspired ethical approaches. Learning outcomes: L01, L05

Academic Writing & Finalising Research Proposal Research not only involves a range of data generation, collection and analysis processes but also typically involves close attention to presentation. This week will focus on how to present your written work as clearly as possible. It will also be an opportunity for you to address any final queries you may have about the research proposal - the second assessment task for the course. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Research Impact and Wrap-Up This is the final class for the course. This will be an opportunity to ask any final questions about the nature of educational research processes and practices. We will also consider the importance of impact and how to ensure our research is impactful for as many audiences as possible. We can also address any final queries re the oral assessment component of the course. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
